controlPoint.name: Access request approved
controlPoint.enforces: OIG request requires manager approval before any grant is executed — the deny-by-default gate.
controlPoint.dataElement: Okta OIG request object: requester, approver, target, timestamps
controlPoint.evidence: Population export of all OIG requests · hash raw response
controlPoint.completenessAccuracy: Two-source reconciliation: OIG requests vs. GitHub grant events
controlPoint.gap: Approver ≠ requester enforced in policy config — evidence the config, not just the tickets.

controlPoint.name: Grant matches approval
controlPoint.enforces: Provisioning bot executes exactly the approved scope — grant compared to request, deltas flagged.
controlPoint.dataElement: Bot execution log: approved scope vs. granted scope
controlPoint.gap: The bot is a trusted actor — its own service account and code path need CM controls (see CM lane).

controlPoint.name: Time-bound · auto-revoke
controlPoint.enforces: Grant carries an expiry; revocation fires without human action. The control is the configuration.
controlPoint.completenessAccuracy: Hash raw config · alert if TTL policy absent

lanes.name: Change management — code to production
lanes.subtitle: the path to prod is the control surface

controlPoint.name: Branch protection · SoD
controlPoint.enforces: Approver ≠ author required before merge; enforced by ruleset, not by process.
controlPoint.dataElement: Branch protection ruleset per in-scope repo
controlPoint.evidence: Config snapshot per repo, hashed, diffed daily
controlPoint.completenessAccuracy: Population = in-scope repo list from product mapping; drift alerts
controlPoint.gap: Admin bypass is the residual — evidence the bypass log and the org-level allowance.

controlPoint.name: Required checks pass
controlPoint.enforces: Security + functional CI checks are required statuses — a failed check mechanically blocks merge.
controlPoint.dataElement: Required status checks config + check-run results
controlPoint.completenessAccuracy: Hash raw responses · classify checks security vs functional

controlPoint.name: Apply bound to reviewed commit
controlPoint.enforces: Terraform applies only from the merged commit via the pipeline — execution moved off laptops, credentials centralized, provenance preserved.
controlPoint.dataElement: Pipeline run: source SHA vs. applied SHA
controlPoint.api: Actions run log + Terraform plan/apply record
controlPoint.completenessAccuracy: Reconcile applied SHA to merged PR population
controlPoint.gap: The value here is provenance and separation of duties — not cryptographic integrity in transit. Say it that way.

controlPoint.name: Drift detection
controlPoint.enforces: Live state vs. IaC state compared on schedule; out-of-band change surfaces as an alert, not at audit.
controlPoint.dataElement: CAI live state vs. Terraform state delta
controlPoint.api: Cloud Asset Inventory export + state file compare
controlPoint.evidence: Delta report per run · alert population
controlPoint.completenessAccuracy: Two-source: live inventory vs. declared state

controlPoint.name: Term feed completeness
controlPoint.enforces: Every termination in the HRIS appears in the deprovisioning queue — the population control everything downstream depends on.
controlPoint.dataElement: Termination feed: worker, type, term date
controlPoint.evidence: Population export · row-count reconciliation vs. HR report
controlPoint.gap: Contractors and collaborators often live outside the HRIS — that population needs its own source.

controlPoint.name: Revoked ≤ 5 business days
controlPoint.enforces: Deprovision timestamp vs. termination date, tested across the full population — no sampling.
controlPoint.dataElement: Deactivation events joined to term feed

controlPoint.name: Downstream revocation verified
controlPoint.enforces: SSO revocation ≠ local account revocation — verify per system where local accounts exist.
controlPoint.dataElement: Per-system account status for terminated users
controlPoint.evidence: Log query per system · exceptions to review
controlPoint.gap: This is where most programs quietly fail — SCIM coverage map determines which systems need it.
